title: The current solution does not pass its build gate
claim: The canonical build fails on analyzer errors in Notifications.cs and LiveEvents.cs.
evidence: `scripts/check.ps1 -Task build` reports IDE0047 at Notifications.cs:105 and CA1826 at LiveEvents.cs:109, with warnings treated as errors.
failure_scenario: CI and clean developer builds stop before producing deployable services or trustworthy test evidence.
recommendation: Fix both analyzer failures and rerun build, lint and tests before advancing phase status.

title: OutcomeUnknown ends the workflow before reconciliation
claim: Runtime exits its only workflow run when Executor reports OutcomeUnknown, although the domain explicitly permits a later conclusive report.
evidence: IncidentWorkflow lines 185-190 escalates and returns for OutcomeUnknown; Incident.RecordExecution lines 520-533 accepts a later result over OutcomeUnknown; Executor emits the provisional result before reconciliation.
failure_scenario: A timed-out rollback later verifies successfully, but no workflow remains to start recovery verification, leaving the incident escalated instead of correctly resolved.
recommendation: Continue waiting after OutcomeUnknown until a conclusive report or execution deadline and add a Temporal regression test.

title: Revocation can be acknowledged after execution starts
claim: Api makes revocation final from a potentially lagging projection before Runtime authoritatively accepts it.
evidence: Api stores Revoked and returns success at lines 240-264; Runtime rejects revocation after ExecutionStart at Incident.cs:461-467; RemediationControlService logs and drops the refusal while returning success.
failure_scenario: An operator sees a successful revocation while the privileged action proceeds because Runtime had already recorded the point of no return.
recommendation: Make Runtime the synchronous authority or retain a pending state until its authoritative acceptance is received.

title: Executor administration endpoints trust unauthenticated callers
claim: Policy and emergency/action control mutations accept an unauthenticated caller and caller-supplied actor identity.
evidence: The routes at lines 38-55 have no authentication/authorization and mutate Executor-owned state directly; they are enabled in Development or by configuration.
failure_scenario: Any reachable process changes execution policy or safety controls while impersonating an operator.
recommendation: Authenticate the Api/operator caller at Executor, derive actor identity from authentication, and audit in the owning service.

title: Runtime trusts unsigned approval-state messages
claim: Runtime applies approval, rejection and revocation payloads without authenticating their producer.
evidence: Lines 28-65 translate bus messages directly into domain commands; all five services receive the same messaging Redis resource and no producer signature is checked here.
failure_scenario: A compromised service publishes a forged operator decision and alters the remediation path.
recommendation: Authenticate producers, restrict these message types to Api, and verify signed provenance for every decision type.

title: Invalid execution commands can poison valid idempotency keys
claim: Executor reserves a predictable external idempotency key before validating the command, plan, policy or attestation.
evidence: Existing keys return at lines 126-136; a new request is durably saved at lines 140-144 before ValidateAsync at line 146; Runtime derives the key from predictable plan identifiers.
failure_scenario: An invalid command arrives first and permanently causes the later legitimate command to replay the stored rejection.
recommendation: Authenticate and validate before reservation, or atomically bind the reservation to validated command identity and permit safe conflicting recovery.

title: Internal query and replay APIs lack caller and tenant enforcement
claim: Owning services expose incident, execution, memory and replay routes without service authentication and often query only by globally supplied IDs.
evidence: Runtime routes at lines 47-68 and AgentWorker routes at lines 26-42 accept no authenticated tenant; PostgresIncidentStore.ListAsync selects all tenants and GetDetailAsync predicates only incident_id. Api filtering is the only current guard.
failure_scenario: A reachable workload enumerates cross-tenant evidence or triggers costly replays without passing through Api authorization.
recommendation: Add service authentication and tenant-scoped contracts/storage predicates; keep Api filtering as defense in depth.

title: Control-plane mutations can commit without an audit record
claim: Executor commits safety-relevant state before Api independently records the audit entry.
evidence: ControlPlaneService awaits Executor mutation calls before writing and committing Api's audit record; the writes cannot share a transaction.
failure_scenario: Executor changes policy or controls, then Api fails before recording who changed it.
recommendation: Write the authoritative mutation audit transactionally in Executor; retain Api request-attempt auditing separately.

title: Concurrent policy publishes bypass expected-version control
claim: Expected-version validation is a non-atomic read then insert.
evidence: PublishAsync checks CurrentAsync and later appends; storage enforces only unique new version strings, not compare-and-swap of the current version.
failure_scenario: Two operators publish from the same base; both receive success and one change silently loses current status.
recommendation: Serialize publication with row locking or an atomic current-version compare-and-swap.

title: Incomplete baseline telemetry can trigger compensation
claim: Recovery validates post-action metadata but uses baseline samples without equivalent completeness and freshness checks.
evidence: BaselineAsync ignores baseline Metadata and averages returned observations; that value can drive a trustworthy CompensationRequired result.
failure_scenario: A truncated low baseline makes recovery look worse and requests compensation instead of returning Inconclusive.
recommendation: Apply the same coverage, completeness, truncation and sample checks to the baseline.

title: Investigation retries repeat model and provider work
claim: No durable per-investigation reservation exists before external work and each retry creates a new execution ID.
evidence: Model/provider work occurs before saving records and committing the outbox; storage uniqueness is only on the newly minted execution ID.
failure_scenario: A database failure after model completion causes redelivery to repeat billable work and potentially produce a different result.
recommendation: Persist a deterministic reservation first and enforce uniqueness by investigation plus role.

title: Executor does not retire cached approval verification keys
claim: Loaded approval keys remain accepted for the process lifetime even after Api stops publishing them.
evidence: ApiApprovalKeys adds unseen keys but never removes/revalidates cached entries; attestation verification does not enforce key metadata lifetime.
failure_scenario: A retired compromised key continues minting approvals accepted by long-running Executor instances.
recommendation: Refresh with removal/revocation semantics and enforce key plus attestation validity windows.

title: Runtime start confirmation does not authenticate Executor
claim: Any HTTP caller with matching identifiers and fencing token can record the point of no return.
evidence: The start-confirmation route directly invokes ConfirmStartAsync with no caller authentication.
failure_scenario: A caller records a false ExecutionStarted event and prevents approval revocation before Executor acts.
recommendation: Require authenticated Executor identity and bind confirmation to a one-time execution request or nonce.

title: Workflow tests omit unknown-outcome reconciliation
claim: Temporal tests do not exercise OutcomeUnknown followed by a conclusive reconciled result.
evidence: The suite drives ActionVerified outcomes and contains no OutcomeUnknown workflow case; Executor-only tests do not protect Runtime lifecycle behavior.
failure_scenario: The cross-component lifecycle defect in F-002 survives while isolated tests remain green.
recommendation: Add a durable workflow regression scenario covering provisional and final execution reports.

title: The phase ledger understates Phase 05–08 implementation
claim: Capabilities now present in the working tree remain described as absent or merely skeletal.
evidence: The ledger lists adversarial verification, policy/revocation, memory/replay/evaluation/postmortems, live updates and control-plane administration as open despite corresponding implementations in the working tree.
failure_scenario: Contributors duplicate implemented work or misread the actual remaining exit criteria.
recommendation: Update Delivered/Open evidence after the tree is green while keeping phase statuses conservative until exit criteria pass.

title: Architecture tests do not enforce project-reference boundaries
claim: The test checks type-level dependencies but not forbidden project or assembly references.
evidence: `HaveDependencyOnAny` is used without inspecting project references or referenced assemblies; the current graph is clean but not mechanically protected.
failure_scenario: A forbidden service reference is added but unused and the architecture suite remains green.
recommendation: Add a solution-level project/assembly reference allowlist test based on ADR-007.
